Serial timeline performed direct probing and then wrote a partial source implementation without delegated child activity.

parallel.requirements: Recognized a clean-room lnav reimplementation task and gathered behavior from the reference binary and bundled docs.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Launched a workflow of 15 behavior-surface explorers and one gaps critic; no task owned implementation.
parallel.implementation: No replacement source implementation was produced; work remained in notes and behavioral experiments.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The artifact packed notes, README, man page, git data, and the original executable, without a new src tree.
parallel.verification: Many probe commands were run, but no integrated implementation build or evaluator-aligned acceptance was completed.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The required implementation was absent, the run timed out, and official evaluation failed at compile time.

serial.requirements: Worked from the same clean-room prompt and probed lnav behavior through CLI experiments and documentation reads.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Single actor handled exploration and then took ownership of implementation in /workspace/src.
serial.implementation: Created C++ modules for regex, utilities, and datetime scanning, but the implementation remained partial.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The artifact included a src tree with several files but did not compile under the official evaluator.
serial.verification: Ran local probes and some compile checks while building components, but no successful final build was delivered.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Timed out with a partial source implementation that still failed official compilation and ran no tests.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the clean-room requirement and the need to infer lnav behavior from the binary and bundled documentation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial worked under the same prompt and recognized that the deliverable needed to be an original executable-like reimplementation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The recognized requirements were materially the same; the difference is that serial later implemented code while parallel kept mapping behavior.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed into 15 behavior surfaces plus a gaps critic, all focused on reports under /workspace/notes.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial remained single-agent and, after probing, declared it would start building and created a source directory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had many observation owners but no implementation owner; serial owned probing and implementation in one control trajectory.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs were scoped to behavior reports and exact observations, with no cross-child implementation API or file contract.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept discoveries in one trajectory and used them directly while creating local C++ support modules.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel transferred observation tasks rather than implementation interfaces; serial avoided inter-agent handoff boundaries.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel produced behavior notes and schema notes but the packed artifact retained the original workspace files and no source implementation tree.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote a regex engine, utility code, and date-time scanner source files into /workspace/src before timing out.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial made a concrete partial implementation; parallel did not implement a replacement program.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The workflow was designed to return report counts and a gaps report, not a compiled or promotable implementation result.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial immediately integrated its own findings by writing files into the final workspace rather than awaiting child returns.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel lifecycle centered on retrieving research artifacts; serial lifecycle centered on local implementation writes.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel suffered shared HOME contamination when a child-installed foo.json was read by unrelated probes as lnav configuration.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no delegation or subagent shared-state surface in its protocol validation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced cross-agent runtime-state contamination; serial avoided that coordination surface but still failed compilation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Official evaluation completed with compile_failed and all 1172 tests marked not_run.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had the same official compile_failed outcome and all 1172 tests not_run despite having source files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Neither produced evaluator-acceptable build output; the verification outcome was the same even though the artifact contents differed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used 37 subagents, over five million tokens, and timed out at closure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no subagents, spent its budget on direct probing and implementation, and also timed out.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both exhausted the time budget, but parallel spent it on fan-out mapping without implementation while serial spent it on a partial implementation path.

outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no discordant official outcome: both completed official evaluation and failed with compile_failed, leaving 1172 tests not run. The substantive task-solving difference is that the parallel run generated behavior-mapping notes without assigning implementation ownership, whereas serial moved into a partial C++ source implementation before timing out.
parallel_contributors: Map-only workflow with no implementation owner left no replacement source tree.
Shared lnav HOME contamination interrupted multiple behavior probes and forced isolated-HOME retries.
serial_contributors: Single-agent control wrote a partial src tree but still did not reach a compilable solution.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial implementation remained incomplete and failed compile; parallel had no implementation to compile.
evaluator_effects: Both outcomes are compile_failed with all tests not_run, so evaluator results do not create a pass/fail contrast.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained patterns describe adverse parallel process episodes and artifact-surface differences

candidates.reason: The parallel work split covered behavior-map child agents and a gaps critic, but no actor was assigned to produce the clean-room implementation demanded by the prompt; the final artifact therefore lacked a source tree.
candidates.realized_consequence: Parallel packaged no replacement source tree and left the evaluator with no implemented code to compile.
candidates.near_match_reason: No Assembly Owner would require implemented components awaiting packaging; here the implementation itself had no owner.

candidates.reason: No separately owned implementation components were created, so there was no integration owner to be missing.
The parallel run lacked implemented components; the earliest unowned object was implementation, not final assembly.
The missing stage was direct implementation ownership, not a staffed pipeline lacking end-to-end coordination.
No mandatory serial preflight blocked implementation; the parent chose a map-only workflow and also probed locally.
Investigation was broadly parallel, not a completed first phase whose returned findings then delayed a staffed implementation phase.
Implementation was not merely underallocated while auxiliary work dominated; it had no owner at all.
High fan-out and timeout were present, but the specific actionable boundary was a plan with no implementation owner.
No single child received the full implementation burden or another overbroad indispensable task.
The children were intentionally briefed to map behavior surfaces, not to implement; no known requirement was omitted from an implementation child brief.
There were no separately owned implementation components whose interfaces diverged.
No specific known finding was shown to disappear through transfer and cause repeated or wrong downstream work.
Reports may have been large, but the retained failure is earlier: no implementation owner existed to consume them.
No receiver acted on a superseded handoff as the cause of an inconsistent implementation step.
The record does not show incompatible child reports reaching the parent and remaining unadjudicated at integration.
The parent did not present the whole task as complete; the run timed out and produced an empty final response.
No replacement or retry episode repeated prior work without inherited checkpoints.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: Interrupted child traces appear as run-end artifacts, not an explicit parent cancellation before a needed implementation result.
No complete promotable implementation candidate existed before closure.
No implementation merge occurred after integrated verification.
No delegated implementation was completed and then left unjoined.
No concrete verifier finding was trapped below the parent as an independent result-lifecycle failure.
No required implementation child failed with its scope left untaken; the implementation scope was never assigned.
Completed behavior reports were not enough to satisfy the task, and the directly corrective boundary remains missing implementation ownership.
The parent actively probed and inspected state; the timeout was not caused by blindly waiting on available results.
No concurrent source-file designs claimed overlapping implemented behavior.
No live agents edited the same source or configuration file with observed reconciliation.
No actor replaced another actor-owned non-entry source module.
No submitted executable or entry-point source was overwritten by another live actor.
No broad cleanup or promotion replaced another actor’s final workspace output.
The observed shared-state problem was a runtime/config artifact leak, not competing writes in a shared implementation workspace.
A parallel child installed a malformed format file into the shared lnav home, and later parent/child probes consumed that generated file as ambient configuration, forcing isolation workarounds.
candidates.realized_consequence: Unrelated lnav probes failed with invalid-format errors until agents switched to private HOME directories.
candidates.near_match_reason: The observed collision was not a shared implementation workspace write; it was leakage of an auxiliary runtime/configuration artifact.

deduplicated_same_label_episodes: Multiple consumers of foo.json were treated as one Artifact Leakage episode because they share the same producer artifact and contamination chain.
suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Critical-Path Starvation and Fan-out Budget Exhaustion were suppressed because the actionable boundary is the missing implementation owner, not budget symptoms.
Unisolated Workspace Writes was suppressed because the concrete shared-state problem was an auxiliary runtime artifact leak.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and 32 Level-3 candidates were audited; no additional independent coordination boundary cleared the retention gate.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: No downstream timeout, lifecycle, context, or write labels were added for consequences already covered by the two retained episodes.
